'''Andoa''' is an extinct [[Zaparoan]] [[language]] of [[Ecuador]] and [[Peru]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Hinton |first1=Leanne |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5zpODwAAQBAJ |title=The Routledge Handbook of Language Revitalization |last2=Huss |first2=Leena |last3=Roche |first3=Gerald |date=2018-03-05 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-317-20085-7 |pages=406 |language=en}}</ref> It was found in the [[Pastaza River]] region of [[Ecuador]] and Peru. It is also known as Shimigae/Semigae and Gae/Gay.{{Citation needed|date=January 2024}} The [[Andoa people]] have integrated into the [[Quechua people|Quechua]] and now speak either [[Canelos-Quichua|Canelos-Quechua]] or [[Spanish language|Spanish]]. The last known speaker, Hipólito Arahuanaza, died in 2012.
